articles.title: Blacksmithing returns to Gretna Green after more than 150 years
articles.summary: Thousands of couples marry at an anvil in Scotland's wedding capital every year - but the traditional craft had disappeared.
articles.body:
Blacksmithing has returned to Scotland's wedding capital for the first time in more than 150 years with the opening of a new forge.

Couples have married at the anvil in Gretna Green for centuries, but the traditional craft had disappeared from the village.

The new forge will offer visitors the chance to practise the skills involved and even allow newly-weds to create a keepsake of their own.

Resident blacksmith Joe Shevelan said it was "incredibly special" to be part of seeing the craft of shaping and joining metal return.

Gretna Green became a popular wedding venue due to its location in the south of Scotland.

The Marriage Act - passed in 1754 in England - outlawed marriages without parental consent if either party was under 21.

However, eloping couples could pop over the border and be married simply by stating their intent in front of witnesses - usually at the blacksmiths.

They would strike the anvil as part of the wedding ceremony - a tradition which has continued to this day.

Over time, blacksmithing gave way to the more lucrative marriage business with about 18% of all Scotland's weddings taking place in Dumfries and Galloway - the majority at Gretna Green.

Joe said he was fulfilling a long-held ambition.

"I decided I wanted to be a blacksmith when I was about 10, I think, I remember telling my mum that that's what I was going to be," he said.

"They didn't let 10-year-olds run around in dangerous workshops - so I had to wait a little while before I could go and study down in Hereford."

He said he had always been fascinated by the craft.

"I think I've always liked the characters in movies and films and books and stuff, not the hero of the story, but the guy who made the hero's sword," he said.

He said the blacksmith always held an "important place" in the local community.

Although modern equipment has made things easier, he said they still struck the anvil and worked in traditional ways.

"Being able to be the blacksmith returning to Gretna after 150 years really is an honour," he added.

Joe said there were more blacksmiths than people might expect, with about 1,800 members of the British Artistic Blacksmithing Association.

He added that he hoped his work at the new forge might add a few more to their number.

"I think inspiring just one person to pick up the craft would be enough for me," he said.

"I'd love the site to develop into something so important to the future of blacksmithing that it lives way longer than I do."

For Michelle Henry, head of attractions and events at Gretna Green Ltd, it is a "full circle moment" for a business which has been family-run since 1825 and will allow couples to create a very special memento.

"Every piece that Joe crafts in the forge is unique so everything they make is unique to them and their marriage," she said.

"So it's really significant that they get to take a piece of Gretna Green away with them as well."

articles.title: Tiger Woods Pleads No Contest to Reckless Driving Charge over Rollover Crash in Florida
articles.summary: STUART, Florida (AP) — Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge and his driver's license was suspended for five years Wednesday following a March rollover crash in Florida, where he initially was accused of driving under the influence.
articles.body:
STUART, Florida (AP) — Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge and his driver's license was suspended for five years Wednesday following a March rollover crash in Florida, where he initially was accused of driving under the influence.

Woods, still one of golf's most influential figures and as recognizable as any athlete in the world, has had a remarkable fall since winning the 2019 Masters for his 15th major. The first person of Black heritage to win the Masters in 1997, his career has been derailed by multiple back and knee surgeries, car crashes and dependence on pain medication .

Court Documents: Tiger Plans to Change Plea in DUI Case (AP)

He was arrested in March after his SUV clipped a truck and rolled over on its side on a beachside residential road near his home on Jupiter Island. A sheriff's report said deputies found two pain pills in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment. He did a Breathalyzer test, which came out negative, but refused to take a urine test.

He pleaded not guilty to the original DUI charge.

Before the hearing in Florida's Marin County on Wednesday, Woods, 50, sat at the defense table looking back at the mostly empty courtroom gallery. He said little as he agreed to the reduced charge and left the courthouse without addressing reporters.

He had arrived with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, President Donald Trump's former daughter-in-law. She sat behind him during the proceedings.

"Tiger is not absolved of accountability and he surrendered his license for the next five years," Mark Steinberg, his longtime manager at Excel Sports told the AP. "He is continuing his treatment and prioritizing all aspects of his health."

Prosecutor says Tiger Woods has a tolerance to pain medicine

The prosecutor in the case said two toxicologists found there was insufficient proof of his impairment and determined Woods had built up a "pharmacological" tolerance after years of using pain pills.

Thomas Bakkedahl, a state attorney, defended his decision to accept the plea, saying, "I did what I think is right."

Prosecutors obtained the golfer's pharmacy records that showed he had a lawful prescription, Bakkedahl said.

The deputy who arrested Woods after the crash found two white pills in his pocket that had markings identifying them as hydrocodone, according to the arrest report. Hydrocodone is an opioid that is prescribed for pain, but it can be addictive.

Woods told the deputy he takes a few prescription medications, according to the report, including "Vicodin" — a brand name painkiller that contains hydrocodone.

He has had numerous surgeries on his legs and back over the last two decades — some to treat cartilage and ligament damage, a ruptured tendon, arthritis, and damaged discs in his back.

At Wednesday's hearing, Woods also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to testing after the crash and was fined $1,500, according to court documents. A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defense. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.

Woods' attorney did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

Body camera footage shows Woods taking out his phone after the crash and telling a deputy, "I was just talking to the president."

Woods can be heard saying, "Thank you so much," as he hangs up and the deputy approaches. It is not clear if Woods was referring to President Donald Trump.

The footage also shows the handcuffed Woods hiccupping, yawning and repeatedly appearing to nod off during the 15-minute ride.

Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle were injured in the crash, according to officials. Woods told a deputy that he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station when he hit the truck.

Woods has been involved in four crashes over the years. He took a leave from the golf tour after the 2009 crash and again after the latest crash and has yet to return to tournament play.

He left the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient treatment facility, according to court records.

Woods made his first public appearance since returning from treatment on June 23 when he introduced the PGA Tour's plans to revamp its schedule for 2028. Woods remained as chair of the tour's Future Competition Committee after his arrest.

It's not clear if Tiger is allowed to drive a golf cart

Judge Darren Steele warned Woods that his driver's license suspension didn't include any exceptions.

"If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would immediately go back to jail," the judge told Woods.

The prosecutor said he was confident that Woods would be spotted if he doesn't heed the message.

"Of all the people in the world who should not get behind the wheel of a car, it's one of the most recognizable people on the planet," Bakkedahl said.

But what wasn't immediately clear is whether Woods can drive a golf cart on a golf course. Bakkedahl told reporters he needed to check on that.

Associated Press Golf reporters Doug Ferguson in Jacksonville, Florida, and John Seewer in Toledo, Ohio, contributed.

Tiger Woods has pleaded guilty to a charge of reckless driving in connection with a March wreck in Jupiter, Florida. As a result, his driver's license will be suspended for five years.

In March, Woods was traveling at a high rate of speed on a two-lane road in Jupiter, Florida, around 2 p.m. when he clipped the trailer of a yard maintenance truck. Woods' vehicle rolled over, though he was able to climb out of it without injury. An officer at the scene indicated that Woods "did exemplify signs of impairment."

Officers described Woods as "lethargic" on the scene and administered roadside tests. He was arrested and transported to the Martin County jail, where he refused a urinalysis test. articles.summary: Tiger Woods has entered a plea agreement for reckless driving after the car crash outside his home in March; Woods' driving licence will be suspended for five years; Woods attended a plea conference hearing at Martin County Courthouse in Florida
articles.body:
The 15-time major champion was arrested in March and spent eight hours in jail, before being bailed, after the Land Rover he was driving rolled over in a collision with a pick-up truck towing a trailer.

Woods previously entered a written plea of not guilty via his lawyers to charges of driving under the influence, property damage and a refusal to submit to testing.

The former world No 1 attended a plea conference hearing at Martin County Courthouse in Florida on Wednesday, where he pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of reckless driving and the refusal to submit an unlawful test.

Judge Darren Steele accepted the plea agreement, which amended the original DUI charge and resolved the refusal to submit a test charge, while Woods also entered a plea to a careless driving citation.

On the reckless driving second offence charge, Woods received a $1,000 (£748) fine and a five-year driving suspension. On the second count, the refusal to submit to a lawful test, he received a $500 (£370) fine.

"There are no exceptions. If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go ​immediately back to jail," Steele told the court.

Woods was ordered to pay the minimum fine for the careless driving citation, which also carries a five-year driving ban to run concurrently with the suspension on the reckless driving charge.

The 50-year-old said little during the hearing. He arrived at the courthouse with Vanessa Trump, his girlfriend and President Donald Trump's former daughter-in-law, who sat behind him during a hearing that lasted under 10 minutes.

He was also fined court costs, according to court documents. A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defense. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.

The police report from the March 27 crash said deputies found two hydrocone pills - used to treat pain - in his pocket, and he showed signs of impairment. It described Woods' movements as slow and lethargic when speaking to deputies at the scene.

The report also said Woods appeared to be sweating, his eyes looked glassy, and his pupils were dilated. Woods managed to crawl out of his car without any injuries and told a deputy he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station when he hit the truck.

Woods has not featured in a professional golf event since missing the cut at The Open in July 2024.

He made his first public appearance since returning from treatment in Switzerland on June 23, when he introduced the PGA Tour's plans to revamp its schedule for 2028. Woods remained as chairman of the PGA Tour's Future Competition Committee after his arrest.

articles.title: La pregunta que queda en el aire: ¿Puede Tiger conducir un buggy?
articles.standfirst: El portavoz del Estado de Florida responde con un “tendremos que investigar eso”
articles.summary: El portavoz del Estado de Florida responde con un “tendremos que investigar eso”
articles.body: Tiger Woods no podrá conducir durante cinco años después de haber cambiado su declaración y aceptar esta sanción y 1.500 dólares de multa por el accidente que sufrió en Júpiter (Florida) en marzo pasado. En la rueda de prensa posterior, surgió una pregunta que ni el propio portavoz del Estado de Florida pudo responder. "¿Podrá Tiger Woods conducir un buggy?", le interrogaron. A lo que el administrativo respondió con un "tendremos que investigar esto". Hay que recordar que un muchos recorridos de golf, los buggys circulan por algunas calles que forman parte de las urbanizaciones. Algunos de los torneos del Champions Tour, la liga para mayores de 50 años del PGA Tour -la edad de Tiger-, se juegan ayudados de buggys por varios golfistas. No hay jurisprudencia, pero en las leyes españolas sí surge alguna comparativa con los patinetes de las ciudades. Según la legislación de nuestro país si se supera la tasa de alcoholemia en un patinete de 0,60 mg/l en aire aspirado o renuncia al test -como hizo Tiger Woods- se está cometiendo un delito contra la seguridad vial (art. 379.2 CP), exactamente igual que en coche. La Fiscalía General del Estado (Circular 2/2024) considera los patinetes eléctricos "vehículos a motor" a efectos penales. En ese caso el juez puede imponer, además de multa o prisión, privación del derecho a conducir de 1 a 4 años, y esa privación afecta a "toda clase de vehículos a motor" — incluye también los patinetes. Durante ese periodo también estaría prohibido y podría constituir un nuevo delito de conducción sin permiso atendiendo al artículo 284 del Código Penal.

articles.title: Good Good Golf CEO, president leave company as fallout from Callaway ad continues
articles.summary: Co-founder Garrett Clark, who shoved a woman for attempting to touch his driver in the since-deleted ad, is reportedly remaining with Good Good and will cont...
articles.body:
Good Good Golf CEO Matt Kendrick and president Joe Flannery have left the brand in the wake of their advertisement with Callaway that generated massive backlash in recent weeks.

Kendrick and Flannery left the company this week, according to multiple reports. An internal memo, via The Athletic , stated that early investor and co-founder Nahid Giga is planning to step in as the company's interim CEO. Both Kendrick and Flannery, according to the memo, left the company of their own accord.

Their departures are the latest after the Good Good Golf-Callaway advertisement that was released last month. Good Good Golf released the ad that showed one of its co-founders, Garrett Clark, shoving a female employee to the ground as she attempted to touch the driver in his golf bag.

The ad was removed the next day, and both Good Good and Callaway have since apologized. Callaway eventually ended its partnership with Good Good and announced that it would donate $1 million to charities aimed at preventing domestic violence. Callaway director of content and production Alex Upegui is also leaving the company.

The PGA Tour has since split with Good Good , and the Good Good Championship this fall will have another title sponsor.

Clark is going to remain with the company and will continue creating content, according to Front Office Sports. Good Good vice president of brand marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was fired this week .

"Despite the recent controversy, the company is seeing online retail growth, continued support from investors, and sees an opportunity to re-engage former retail partners in the future," a Good Good spokesperson told Front Office Sports on Wednesday .

Flannery previously led TravisMatthew before landing at Good Good, and he also spent time with The North Face and Score Sports, according to The Athletic. He was in his first few days with the company.

Kendrick had been Good Good's CEO since 2020. He went on a social media rant last week , criticizing Callaway for approving the ad in the first place and saying he thought the company dropped Good Good as part of a "coordinated media blitz." He has since deleted some of his social media posts, clarified that members of the marketing team who approved the ad on Good Good's end are no longer with the company and said Good Good has no intention of suing Callaway after all.

American golf brand Good Good has sacked two senior executives following backlash over an advert which showed a woman being pushed to the ground after reaching for a club.

The company, whose YouTube channel has 2.1m subscribers, said it had parted ways with chief executive Matt Kendrick and president Joe Flannery following the release of the advert created for golf club manufacturer Callaway.

Good Good vice-president of brand and marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was sacked earlier this week.

Nahid Giga, a board member and investor in Good Good, has been installed as interim CEO.

Last month Good Good and Callaway removed the advert and issued apologies.

Callaway ended its partnership with Good Good and said it was donating $1m (£736,000) to organisations working to prevent violence against women and support victims.

Good Good, whom Callaway has worked with since 2023, has stepped away from its sponsorship of a PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas, in November.

Good Good products have also been pulled from the shelves of several retailers.

The advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark rushing over to Alexis Miestowski - a professional golfer and regular content creator for Good Good - and pushing her to the ground before shouting: "Do not touch my new driver."

The brand, which has become one of the largest content creators in golf, launched its YouTube channel 2020. Regular clips include men and women competing in various golf challenges.

Good Good also creates made-for-TV shows as well as adverts for golf clothing and other merchandise.

articles.title: Zack Polanski says he'll run for former PM Starmer's seat in by-election
articles.summary: The Green Party leader intends to run in the Holborn and St Pancras seat following Sir Keir Starmer's resignation as MP.
articles.body:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski has confirmed he wants to stand in the by-election brought about by Sir Keir Starmer's resignation as an MP.

Polanski, who is currently a London Assembly member but not a member of Parliament, said he was "so excited by the prospect" of being the first Green MP for Holborn and St Pancras.

The Greens are targeting the seat, until now a Labour stronghold, after coming second to Labour in the area in local elections earlier this year.

Sir Keir announced on Tuesday that he was quitting as MP for the London constituency, two months after he stood down as prime minister, setting up a challenging by-election for his successor Andy Burnham.

In comments to the Camden New Journal on Thursday morning, Polanski said: "I have lived and worked in this community over many years, I know it well and I love it.

"It represents so many of the things that make London so special. I am so excited by the prospect of representing this place in Parliament."

He added: "It's a clear fight between Labour and the Green Party."

In order to officially be the Green candidate for the seat, Polanski needs to be selected by local party members - something his comments suggest will happen.

But there have been reports in recent days of splits among local Green activists, some of whom are said to favour a Palestinian candidate or a pro-Gaza independent.

Andrew Feinstein, the independent runner-up to Sir Keir in the constituency at the 2024 general election, said he believes Polanski will be an "excellent candidate".

Writing on X, Feinstein said: "Unfortunately I am not in a position to stand this time round."

He said the Camden People's Alliance will meet next week to formally decide its position, adding: "This is a crucial time for progressives in Camden and across the country to be united."

A date has not yet been set for the by-election.

The stakes were already high for Labour at this by-election, because it offers an early test of Burnham's ability to stave off the Green threat in inner-city constituencies.

With Polanski's candidacy, the stakes are even higher for the Greens, to see whether they make good on their leader's oft-stated ambition to replace Labour.

Polanski said a Green victory would be a "clear message that we won't sit by as we get poorer and extreme wealth is concentrated at the very top."

Keir Starmer announces he is standing down as MP

Sir Keir had been MP for the area since 2015, but said he was quitting to focus on a role in international affairs.

The former prime minister had previously said he would stay on as an MP until the next UK general election, which is not due until 2029.

He said it was the "right time" for him to "pass the baton to a successor".

"I will now focus on other things and that will be international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast-changing world," he said, adding he would also continue his work combatting violence against women and girls.

Sir Keir became prime minister after winning a landslide majority at the 2024 election, but quit No 10 after pressure from Labour MPs to stand aside.

Labour has not decided its candidate to potentially take on Polanski, with applications closing on Friday.

articles.title: Good Good Golf CEO, president quit amid advertisement controversy
articles.summary: The advertisement faced severe backlash and prompted calls for a boycott of products from Callaway, which co-branded it.
articles.body:
The top brass at golf media platform Good Good Golf have left the company in the wake of severe backlash over an advertisement that showed a man shoving a woman to the ground and telling her not to touch the club.

The company parted ways with CEO Matt Kendrick and President Joe Flannery, Good Good’s head of finance and operations Alex Puchala announced on Wednesday.

The commercial, released online last month before being pulled, showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver. It prompted calls to boycott products from Callaway, which co-branded the advertisement.

Callaway issued an apology for the advertisement, and Callaway chief executive Chip Brewer said in a statement on Tuesday that the company had launched an investigation into how the advertisement – produced by golf media firm Good Good Golf – had been approved.

“Last week Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver,” Brewer said in a statement.

“The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: We are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence or threatening behaviour of any kind … I assure you we will learn from this and do better.”

Nahid Giga, a board member and investor in Good Good, was installed as the interim CEO of the company, while Vice President of Brand and Marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was fired earlier this week.

Good Good was launched as a YouTube channel in 2020 and is now among the largest content creators in the sport, featuring eight men and four women competing in golf and various challenges. It has made-for-TV shows, apparel and other merchandise.

The company had said the controversial video was meant to parody the horror movie Obsession. But the criticism was immediate and relentless.

The video was deleted the same day it was posted on August 20, but it continued to make the rounds on social media and apologies from Good Good and Callaway had little effect.

“We were disappointed with what we saw,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said last week of the response from Good Good. “The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all.”

Good Good pulled its title sponsorship of a new PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas, later this year. The tour said the tournament will still be played.

Callaway ended its relationship with Good Good, and retailers including Golf Galaxy and its parent company, Dick’s Sporting Goods, removed the company’s merchandise from their shelves. Golf Channel cancelled a new season of its Big Break reality series in which it partnered with Good Good.

Garrett Clark, a Good Good founder and the man who shoves the woman in the video, posted an eight-minute video in which he called the commercial in question “the worst ad known to man” and “not what we stand for”.

articles.title: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff
articles.summary: Jon Rahm's return to the PGA Tour looks unlikely as LIV Golf restructures, leaving the Spaniard with $150 million owed and no clear path home.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm stands at a crossroads that could define the rest of his career. The two-time major champion's future with LIV Golf looks shaky as the league tries to secure new funding. Reports suggest the breakaway tour might not keep him. This isn't just a small contract dispute. It involves a massive $150 million sum still owed to the Spanish star. As the league restructures, the man many called their flagship player might be walking away. The situation creates a ripple effect across professional golf, leaving fans wondering where the 31-year-old will play next season.

When Rahm jumped to the rebel tour in late 2023, he signed a deal loaded with cash. Per multiple reports, he is still owed around $150 million from that multi-year contract. That figure makes his position unique and complicated. As LIV Golf fights to bring in a new lead investor, reportedly BC Partners, the league's financial math changes. His contract now looks out of bounds for the new owners. Losing such a high-profile talent would be a huge blow to the league's credibility. LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil admitted the stakes were high. To reach and complete this transaction is the sole focus of our efforts. Without the players, that becomes very difficult, O'Neil said, as reported by reports. The pressure is on to close the deal while keeping stars like Rahm happy.

Despite the drama, Rahm kept his own counsel when asked about his plans at the season finale in Indianapolis. He dodged the big questions with a light-hearted comment. "I'm mainly looking forward to a haircut tomorrow morning at 10 a.m. because I need one badly," Rahm said. While he joked about grooming, the reality is stark. According to reports, LIV management has already acknowledged that the Legion XIII captain will depart the breakaway tour. The writing seems to be on the wall for his time in the league.

The door back to the PGA Tour isn't wide open either. Earlier this year, the American circuit introduced a Returning Members Program. Rahm was eligible to use it, but he did not follow up. Only Brooks Koepka has returned home so far. Now, the path is closed. "There's no current plans for a Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said at East Lake, as per reports. This statement confirms that Rahm cannot simply walk back into the fold. His sole path to return involves completing a full season on the DP World Tour and securing qualification via the Race to Dubai standings.

This potential departure signals a shift in the power dynamic between the tours. If Rahm leaves LIV, it proves that even massive signing bonuses cannot guarantee long-term loyalty when business models shift. The $150 million owed creates a financial hurdle that LIV might not clear with new investors. For the PGA Tour, the lack of a Returning Member Program shows they are holding firm on their stance. They want players to earn their way back through performance, not just sign a waiver. This forces Rahm into a difficult spot where he must choose between a tour that might not want him and a tour that might not be able to pay him fully.

The immediate future remains unclear for the Spaniard.

articles.title: 10 days until Saints opener: Every player to wear the No. 10 jersey

articles.body:
Only 10 days remain until the New Orleans Saints ' 2026 season opener. New Orleans will start the year on the road when it travels to face the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Sept. 13. New kicker Daniel Carlson will wear No. 10 for the Saints. Carlson is an eight-year veteran brought in during training camp to stabilize the kicking position. He'll become the 16th player to wear that number in franchise history. Our countdown to kickoff series continues with a look at each.

Charlie Durkee was not only the first to wear No. 10 for the Saints, but also the franchise's first kicker. Durkee wore No. 10 during the first two years of the team's existence, then had No. 15 when he returned to the organization for two years in 1971. In No. 10, Durkee converted 33 of 69 field goal attempts and was perfect on 54 extra points.

Julian Fagan was the punter with New Orleans for three seasons, averaging 41.6 per kick with a long of 71 yards.

Bobby Douglass was brought to New Orleans in 1976 with Archie Manning out for the year with a shoulder injury. Douglass split time with Bobby Scott at quarterback that year, starting six of 11 games with a 2-4 record. He also made two starts the following year, as his overall statistics with the Saints were 1,418 passing yards, five touchdowns, 11 interceptions, and a 48.8% completion percentage.

Steve Mike-Mayer and Tom Jurich were two of four kickers that the Saints used in 1978, both wearing No. 10. In 10 games combined, they were an abysmal 6 of 16 on their field goal attempts. Brian Hansen and Doug Brien each had far greater kicking success during their respective times with New Orleans. Hansen, a punter, had a 42-yard average in five seasons and 76 games with New Orleans to start his 15-year NFL career. Brien was with the Saints for six years and 88 games. Over that span, he had a 99.3% success rate on extra points and 82.6% conversion on field goals. He is fourth in franchise history for successful field goals and third in field goal percentage among those with over 70 attempts. These two specialists also rank first and second for most games played in No. 10 by a New Orleans player.

Jamie Martin was the first backup to Drew Brees with the Saints. Martin backed up Brees for two years, but only saw action in the 2006 season finale, completing 16 of 24 passes for 208 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Chase Daniel also spent time as a Brees backup and sideline confidant. Daniel also saw very little time over his four years in that role, completing 7 of 9 attempts for 55 yards.

Brandin Cooks is the highest-drafted player by the Saints to wear No. 10. The 20th selection in Round 1 of the 2014 NFL Draft, Cooks had a good rookie year with 550 receiving yards in 10 games until shortened by injury. He'd follow that up by leading New Orleans with 84 receptions for 1,138 yards in 2015 and 78 catches for a team-high 1,178 yards in 2016. Included in that 2016 total was a 98-yard touchdown reception, the longest play from scrimmage in Saints franchise history. During the 2017 offseason, New Orleans traded Cooks to the New England Patriots for first- and third-round choices in return that turned out to be Ryan Ramczyk and Trey Hendrickson. Cooks returned to the Saints in the 2025 offseason after playing with four different teams in an eight-year stretch. The reunion lasted 10 games until Cooks was released and finished the year with the Buffalo Bills.

Tre'Quan Smith was expected to replace at least some of Cooks' production when he was drafted in the third round in 2018 out of UCF. That turned out to be far from the case. Smith was with the Saints for five years and played 67 games. He was never a factor in traffic, incapable of getting consistent separation, and often invisible within the offense. His overall statistics were 131 receptions for 1,764 yards and 18 touchdowns.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling was picked up off waivers in 2024 after injuries decimated the New Orleans receiving corps. He ended up being the only viable receiving threat for the team over the last half of the year, catching 17 passes for 385 yards and two touchdowns before departing as a free agent during the 2025 offseason.

Now getting his turn in the 10 jersey is Daniel Carlson, breaking the string of wide receivers to wear the uniform. Carlson has been one of the most consistent kickers in the NFL during his eight-year career. He'll be expected to deliver those same kinds of results in New Orleans for a team desperate for kicking stability.

articles.title: Caleb Surratt Chases DP World Tour Card With Surprise Poland Debut
articles.summary: LIV Golf's Caleb Surratt skips the usual path to compete on the HotelPlanner Tour in Poland, aiming to secure a DP World Tour card as the 2026 season approac...
articles.body:
The golf world is watching a quiet but significant shift as young talent seeks stability. Caleb Surratt, a 22-year American pro linked to Jon Rahm's Legion XIII squad, is making a surprise move. He is heading to Poland for his debut on the HotelPlanner Tour. This comes right after the LIV Golf season ended prematurely. The timing is critical. With the future of the LIV league uncertain, players are hedging their bets. Surratt isn't waiting around for a plan that might not materialize. He is taking action to secure his own path. The goal is clear: earn a DP World Tour card. This card offers a guaranteed spot on a major tour, something LIV can't promise right now. The move signals a pragmatic approach for a young player who has already shown he can compete at the highest level.

Surratt's season has been packed with big moments. His U.S. Open debut occurred in June, followed by participation in the 154th Open at Royal Birkdale during July. On the DP World Tour, he completed three starts while never missing a cut. Last December, he secured a top-ten finish at the Crown Australian Open. More recently, he tied for 13th at the Danish Golf Championship. Despite these successes, he finds himself on the second tier of European golf this week. The reason is simple. He needs more playing opportunities to build his ranking. According to reports, Surratt revealed his primary goal just days after the LIV season wrapped up. In an interview with the HotelPlanner Tour, he stated, "Right now, I'm trying to pursue a DP World Tour card." He added that he is hoping for more chances this year to play his best golf.

The HotelPlanner Tour's Rosa Challenge Tour in Poland represents the next step. Surratt is set to make his debut on Thursday. He expressed genuine enthusiasm about the opportunity. "I'm excited," he said. "It's my first time here in Poland and it's a pretty sweet golf course so I'm very excited, and very fortunate to be given a spot and an opportunity to compete this week." His recent form gives him confidence. He remarked, "I was fortunate to play well in Denmark a few weeks ago and was fortunate to get a spot in that as well." He admits he wishes he could have capitalized better on past chances, but he is focused on the present. "My game has been solid," he added. The major debuts this year put a fire inside him. He sees what he is capable of and wants to keep working toward it. When you've stood on the tee at Royal Birkdale, a course in Poland might feel like a step back, but the math behind the card chase tells a different story.

His current standing shows why this move matters. Surratt currently holds the 167th spot on the 2026 Road to Mallorca Rankings. A positive result this week could improve his standings significantly. It might even put him in contention to earn one of the 15 available DP World Tour cards. This is a high-stakes week for a player who has already proven he can handle pressure. The DP World Tour reported that he is not resting on his laurels. He is putting in the hard work to remain consistent. His focus is on what he can do to help him play good golf. He has a goal in mind towards the end of the year. He just needs to take it one day at a time.

This tournament serves as a foundation for career security. The LIV Golf League faces serious questions regarding its future. The Saudi Public Investment Fund pulled its backing, creating a shaky foundation. Players are seeing the writing on the wall. They aren't waiting to see what happens next. Surratt's move to the HotelPlanner Tour is a smart play. It gives him a chance to compete on a tour that is definitely running. It is a way to keep his game sharp while the LIV situation remains in limbo. For a young player like Surratt, who has already competed in two majors, the goal is to build a long-term career. The DP World Tour card is the golden ticket. It opens doors to the biggest events and the best fields. By playing in Poland, he is giving himself a fighting chance. He is not betting on hope. He is betting on a scheduled tee time.

The immediate focus is the tournament in Poland. Surratt is set to make his debut on Thursday. The event is the Rosa Challenge Tour. It is a crucial test for his ranking. A good performance here could be the difference between getting a card and missing out. The 2026 Road to Mallorca Rankings are the key metric. Every shot counts. The next concrete step is the competition itself. The event runs this week in Poland. Surratt is ready. He has the game. He has the drive. Now he needs the result. The golf world will be watching to see if he can capitalize on this rare opportunity.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler's caddie details conversation about potential $1 billion LIV Golf offer, why he'd decline
articles.summary: Caddie Ted Scott reveals Scottie Scheffler's bold response when asked about a potential $250 million LIV Golf offer as the world's top player.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler recently took over the top spot on the PGA Tour's career money list with more than $130 million earned. It's fair to say that the 30-year-old who has already taken home $10 million more than Tiger Woods did in his career is doing just fine financially, but as his caddie, Ted Scott, recently explained, it's not all about the money for Scheffler. Scheffler became the No. 1 player in the world in March 2022, amid LIV Golf's efforts to lure players away from the PGA Tour, and just three months before the then Saudi-backed circuit's inaugural event. Scott began caddying for Scheffler in November 2021, and having been in the partnership for less than six months at the time, he was still very much in the feeling-things-out stage with his new boss, but one conversation very much set the tone. "When I first started working for him, he was 19th in the world, and he had a white golf bag," Scott said, referring to Scheffler, on a recent appearance on PGA Tour Radio. "I didn't know him that well, and I asked him, I was like: 'Why don't you have sponsors?' "He's like, 'Well, because I just want to play with the equipment that I want to play.' And I was like, 'Okay.' And then I remember whenever all the LIV stuff was going on, you know, he was number one in the world at the time, I didn't know, but I said, 'They're probably going to offer you like $250m to go over there.' "And he says, 'I don't care what they offer me. They can offer me a billion dollars. I'm going to play where the best players are because I just want to beat people.'" Scott went on to admit that it was at that moment he realized just how differently Scheffler is wired. While Scott already had a stellar resume as a caddie before joining forces with Scheffler, having been on the bag for both of Bubba Watson's Masters victories, he and Scheffler have turned into a two-headed monster over the last half-decade. Scott has been on the bag for each of Scheffler's 22 PGA Tour wins, dating back to his first in February 2022, plus the four major championships Scheffler has won at this point in his young career. articles.title: After Years of Mocking the DC Flop, Ryan Reynolds Now Says ‘I Owe Everything’ to Green Lantern
articles.summary: After years of poking fun at Green Lantern, Ryan Reynolds admitted he owes his career and personal life to the infamous 2011 DC superhero movie.
articles.body:
Ryan Reynolds has spent over a decade mocking his notorious 2011 comic book movie flop, Green Lantern , perhaps most famously by including a meta post-credits scene in Deadpool 2 where the merc with a mouth goes back in time to blow out Reynolds’ brains all over a copy of the Green Lantern screenplay. Now, with the HBO series Lanterns out, the actor seems to have developed an appreciation for his DC film, declaring, “I owe my entire career to that movie.”

Speaking on the red carpet at the premiere of his new movie Mayday , Reynolds was asked by Entertainment Tonight if he’d ever consider making a cameo in Lanterns.

"I would totally do a cameo in that," Reynolds said. "I love it. I learned so much making that movie. And I know what you're thinking, you're thinking, 'Oh, learned what not to do.' In part, yes. But also, any time you're making something that large, there are core lessons that come of it.”

“I owe my entire career to that movie. I owe everything to that,” Reynolds said. “Everything about it was a gift that keeps on giving. And I really enjoyed the experience of making it."

Reynolds also met his wife, Blake Lively, on that film. He played Hal Jordan opposite Lively as played Carol Ferris.

Reynolds’ history of poking fun at Green Lantern is lengthy, including trolling fans that his Green Lantern was in the Snyder Cut . Green Lantern director Martin Campbell has expressed his regrets about the film, but thinks it “would’ve been great” had Reynolds scripted it .

articles.title: Ron DeSantis goes to bat for Tiger Woods, MLB announcer calls out 'woke' team & Jena Sims in a 'Chili's' dress
articles.summary: Keith Hernandez calls out the Rays for being woke, while Tiger Woods' golf cart privileges during probation get a response from Ron DeSantis.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com. Hey, you ... look alive! There's college football on TV tonight. Actual college football. The real thing. It's here! Week 1 is here. Arkansas Pine-Bluff-Missouri doesn't do it for you? Fine! How about some Colorado-Georgia Tech?! Remember when Deion Sanders was all anyone could talk about for the first month of the season back in 2023? We followed the Buffs like they were the Nick Saban-led Crimson Tide. If I remember correctly, we stayed up till 2 a.m. to watch them squeak out a triple-overtime win over Colorado State. THE COLORADO BUFFALOES ARE ONCE AGAIN GETTING ROASTED ONLINE FOR LOOKING LIKE A POP WARNER TEAM Perhaps that should've been our first sign that they weren't very good. But still, what an incredible time in college football. Tonight, another season kicks off. Let's roll. Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Mets broadcaster (and Seinfeld star!) Keith Hernandez calls out the Tampa Bay Rays for being WOKE! And he's right. What else? I've got Jena Sims debuting her new Chili's dress, Ryan Reynolds saying, quite possibly, the dumbest thing on the internet today (that's a HIGH bar to clear), and the big issue down here in Florida today? Can Tiger Woods still drive a golf cart during his probation? Our great governor weighs in! Grab you whatever the heck you need to get you through the next few hours before Week 1 officially kicks off, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap! DeSantis leads the way, again! Look at that big, beautiful board. Welcome back, college football! We've got Colorado-Georgia Tech tonight, and Miami-Stanford tomorrow as the two big appetizers before the weekend. I don't know if anyone saw Stanford's crowd last weekend for Week 0, but ... Lordy. The Hurricanes should win by a billion. I'd offer some analysis here but I have no clue which players are on which team at this point because college football is so upside down at the moment. You know how LSU spent the day? In court, against the SEC, over recruiting NFL players. And they have a game against Clemson in two days! What a time to be alive. OK, let's get this class started down here in Florida, where Tiger Woods recently entered a plea deal over his car crash earlier this year and had his license suspended for the next five years. Probably not a bad move. The big question? Will he still be allowed to drive golf carts? He certainly should be, according to Ron DeSantis! Let's stay in Florida and check in on the Devil Rays For those wondering, yes, Tiger will be allowed to drive a golf cart on the course over the next five years. Per Florida law, as long you're at least 18, you can operate a golf cart without a license. That applies to anyone, Tiger's attorney, Thomas Bakkedahl, told the AP in an email. Phew! Now we can all sleep tonight. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Look, obviously I'm making light of a serious situation involving Tiger. I grew up watching Woods every chance I could. He's the reason I started watching golf. Watching him win the 2019 Masters is still one of my favorite sports memories of all time. That being said, he's an idiot who refuses to hire a driver, even though he knows how much of a loose cannon he can be. If he screws this up, I'm officially out. Given his track record over the last 15 years, I'll be holding my breath. OK, for those of us who can drive, let's cut across the state and head to St. Pete, where the Rays caught a stray from Mets announcer Keith Hernandez during yesterday's game: Jena Sims, Ryan Reynolds & is this the loudest F-bomb ever? Do y'all remember when they were the Tampa Bay Devil Rays? Man. It was such a simpler time. I can't believe they nixed the "devil" part of it because it was deemed too satanic a full decade after expansion. I grew up watching some great Devil Rays teams ... And by that, I mean some of the worst baseball teams of my lifetime. But man, they had some ELITE names: All players who were far past their primes, but still had just enough gas in the tank to make things interesting. Fun fact: Wade Boggs hit the first EVER home run in Devil Rays history! Man, we had it so good. Peak time in sports history. OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night. First up? I'm not an '80s kid, so this isn't exactly my wheelhouse. I assume we have a ton of '80s folks in class today, though, so I'm speaking directly to you ... Is Ryan Reynolds a moron? "The 80s was a brutal, brutal time for people. It was a f—ing mess and people forget that. It was a tremendous strife. Socio political tensions everywhere. We were still pretty fresh off a Cuban missile crisis, which was only 15-20 years before." WHAT?! I was born in '93, so I don't have a leg to stand on here, but all I hear about the '80s was how great they were. Never once, in my life, have I heard a single person say anything bad about the 1980s. Not one bad thing. By the way, I'm the same way with the '90s, so I get we can all be biased, but still. There is just no way folks in the '80s were still emotionally triggered by the Cuban Missile Crisis, which ended in — checks notes — 1962. 1962! Hilarious. It's amazing how dumb Hollywood elites are. They never, ever cease to amaze me. Next? Let's check in on my Red Sox, who STINK right now: Yep. If that's not the loudest F-bomb of all time, it has to be up there. I don't know that I've heard a louder one, and I cover these things like the OJ trial. I LOVE a good F-bomb caught on a hot mic. I can't remember one with more violence behind it. OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. Let's all go gamble on some college football tonight and start this season with a bang. Take us home, Jena Sims!
